resolutions.researcher_notes: Operating: Eni PR (18 Aug 2019) states the new 216 km / 30" pipeline was started up and Zohr production reached 2.7 bcfd, i.e. the line is in service. NS Energy confirms field on stream since Dec 2017 with the pipelines transporting gas to El-Gamil. Two independent origins (Eni operator PR vs GlobalData/NS Energy). Value fully supported.

Fuel=Gas: Zohr is the largest gas discovery in Egypt/Mediterranean; both sources describe it as a gas field feeding gas-treatment trains, and the pipelines carry gas (bcfd production). Two independent origins. Value fully supported.

StartYear1=2019: Eni PR dates the start-up of the 216 km 30" pipeline to 18 August 2019; the Enterprise Arabic article (Mar 2019, via Wayback) reports Eni completing/energising the Zohr-to-Damietta/El-Gamil line in April 2019. Two independent origins agree on 2019. Note: the FIELD first-gas was Dec 2017 (NS Energy) — 2019 is specific to this pipeline, so the value is correct for the segment.

LengthKnown=216 km: Eni PR states 'a 216 km long' 30" pipeline; NS Energy states 'two 216km-long and 30in-diameter pipelines'. Offshore-technology.com also cites a 216 km 30" line. Eni is an independent origin from GlobalData/NS Energy. Value fully supported.
FuelSource=Zohr Field: both sources state the pipelines carry gas produced from the Zohr field (Shorouk Block) to the onshore plant. Two independent origins. Value fully supported.

Start=Shorouk concession (offshore Mediterranean) → End=El-Gamil, Port Said. NS Energy contains all tokens verified individually: 'Shorouk', 'Gamil', 'Port Said'. Enterprise Arabic article (Wayback) independently contains الجميل (El Gamil), بورسعيد (Port Said), ظهر (Zohr) and دمياط (Damietta). Two independent origins (one en, one ar). Sheet spelling 'Al Gamil' = El-Gamil; value supported.

CONTRADICTION FLAG — no source supports the stated ownership split (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co/EGAS 48% + Eni SpA 26% + Naturgy 13% + SEGAS 13%). Documented structures do not match: the Zohr FIELD contractor group is Eni 50% / Rosneft 30% / BP 10% / Mubadala 10% (Eni PR), with EGAS holding the state 50% at concession level; the SEGAS/Damietta LNG plant is Eni 50% / EGAS 40% / EGPC 10% (Eni 2020 settlement, Wikipedia SEGAS LNG). Naturgy (ex-Unión Fenosa Gas) exited Damietta in the 2020/2021 Eni settlement and has no documented pipeline stake. The 48/26/13/13 figures appear to be an unsourced/garbled blend and could not be corroborated by any independent source. Left UNRESOLVED for Update review — recommend re-deriving pipeline ownership (likely EGAS + Petrobel/PetroShorouk operators) rather than citing a fabricated split.
